title: Private label structural penetration and premium own-label tiers (Europe)

title: Cost-of-living squeeze, round two: energy-shock inflation, entrenched value-seeking and wallet shift to services
mech: Price/mix (promo depth, downsizing limits, trade-down); volume in discretionary personal care
cats: LHC 3-5 (LAD 5); Hair 3; Body 3
desc: The squeeze did not end with the 2024-25 rate cuts: after the Middle East war began in late February 2026, euro-area inflation returned to 3.3% in August 2026 (energy +14.3%) and the ECB raised rates on 11 June 2026 citing the war. BCG's June 2026 survey finds 53% of Europeans worried about daily finances (40% in 2024) and expects the pullback to persist even if conditions improve; McKinsey expects more than three-quarters of consumers worldwide to keep trading down. HCB's own Q2 2026 shows the new form of the squeeze: price -0.5%, volume +2.1%. Two constraints tighten it: FMCG shelf inflation is only 1.1% (NIQ EU5, 13 weeks to May 2026) against direct-material inflation in the high single digits, and shrinkflation-disclosure laws (France since July 2024, Italy since April 2025, Austria since April 2026; the Bremen court's Milka ruling of May 2026) remove covert downsizing as a lever. Retail's share of EU private consumption fell for a fourth year (31.9%) as wallets move to services and travel. Premium bifurcation holds: NIQ Premium+ is 28.2% of Western European FMCG value and growing 4.1%.

title: Sub-replacement fertility and population decline (developed-market volume erosion)
mech: Volume (fewer children, population decline after the 2029 EU peak)
cats: LHC FCN/FCA/HDW 4; Hair 2-3
desc: EU total fertility fell to 1.34 in 2024 (lowest in the series), Japan at a new record low and Korea 0.80 in 2025 (Korea rising for a second year), US births -1% in 2025. The EU population peaks at 453m in 2029 (EUROPOP2025) and is only 1.5% lower by 2050; East Asia shrinks faster but is a small HCB exposure. The old base's household story was wrong: EU average household size has been flat at 2.3 since 2014 (Germany 2.0 since 2009) and household counts still rise to 2035 (Germany 42.7m in 2025 to 43.2m, Destatis). Atomisation therefore raises loads per capita; the genuine headwinds are fewer children (fewer kid-related loads, lower soil) and post-2029 population decline, which compound mainly beyond the horizon.
